answer: Latency triangulation: every epoch, five verifier nodes in different regions send an agent fresh nonces and time the replies. 1) Round-trip times locate the machine, much as echoes reveal the shape of a canyon. 2) Accounts whose timing fingerprints match are treated as one host and split a single reward. 3) Nonces are new each round, so recorded replies can't be replayed. A farm in one ferrous server rack earns one payout; posing as 1,000 agents means renting ~1,000 machines in distinct places at ~$5/month each. A sonnet per account can't hide where it sits, so the attack stops paying.
